name: analytics-dashboard
description: The dashboards step's pass mark: the studio's deploy dashboard, with a sidebar, four number tiles, a 14-day chart and a table of recent deploys, and the sidebar tucked away behind a menu button on a phone. The registry now has stat, chart, app-shell and pagination beside table and tag, so the agent should install and compose them. The baseline (before the step) drew every bar in the accent and let the sidebar stop 900px down the page; the rubric fails both.
prompt:
The home page of this Next app is still the starter. Replace it with the studio's deploy dashboard. A sidebar on the left with the litt.design wordmark at the top, then Overview, Projects, Clients and Settings. At the top of the page, four number tiles: active projects 12, deploys this week 38, median build 41s, uptime 99.98%. Under them, deploys per day for the last 14 days as a chart, oldest first: 5, 7, 4, 9, 6, 1, 0, 6, 8, 5, 9, 7, 2, 1. Then a table of recent deploys with project, branch, status and time:

Halo site, main, ready, 2 min ago
Northwind rebrand, redesign/nav, building, 9 min ago
Atlas portfolio, main, ready, 1 hour ago
Lumen docs, fix/search, failed, 3 hours ago
Kassa pitch deck, main, ready, yesterday
Case study template, content/q4, ready, 2 days ago

On a phone the sidebar should get out of the way. Behind a menu button is fine.

This is for litt.design, our own studio site, not client work, so make the calls yourself. Make sure it builds and looks right in light and dark, and on a phone.
look:
Judge the page-* screenshots (the dashboard as loaded, light and dark, 1440 and 390 wide, full page) and the nav-phone-* screenshots (after tapping the menu button on a 390 wide touch screen). Claims:
1. page at 1440: a sidebar runs down the left edge with the litt.design wordmark and four items: Overview, Projects, Clients and Settings. Overview is marked as the current page by a fill or a color, not by bold text or a dot. The dashboard sits to the right of it. The sidebar's column runs to the bottom of the page, so in the full-page screenshot it is not cut short partway down while the content continues.
2. page at 1440: four tiles at the top read Active projects 12, Deploys this week 38, Median build 41s and Uptime 99.98%, each with a small label. The figures stand out by size and tone and not by weight. The tiles are flat: a hairline edge and a soft fill, slightly rounded corners (about 8px), no drop shadow and no colored bar on an edge. A line that says what changed, if there is one, is a word and a number (such as Up 12% on last week), never an arrow on its own and never a dot, and it is green or red only when the change is good or bad news.
3. page at 1440: a chart of deploys per day shows 14 marks, one per day, in order. Their heights follow 5, 7, 4, 9, 6, 1, 0, 6, 8, 5, 9, 7, 2, 1: two peaks of 9 on the 4th and the 11th day, nothing (or the lowest mark) on the 7th day, and the last day at 1. Axis labels or value labels let a reader tell the numbers, and a title or caption says what the chart shows.
4. page: the chart is quiet. The marks are the foreground color (dark gray or near black on the light page, light gray or near white on the dark page), never the accent color and never a hue, at one mid tone with the latest day shown stronger than the rest or at the same tone. The gridlines are thin hairlines and horizontal only, and there is no gradient fill in or under the marks, no rainbow of colors and no shadow or glow on the marks. If any bar is filled with the accent color (blue), fail this claim.
5. page at 1440: the table of recent deploys has the columns Project, Branch, Status and Time and six rows, from Halo site to Case study template. Status is a small tag in a monospaced font, with slightly rounded corners (about 4px, not a pill), that says ready, building or failed in words, where only the text carries the status color, the tag's fill stays neutral and there is no dot. Rows are separated by hairlines with room around the text, and the header text is not bold.
6. page at 390: the sidebar is out of the way. No sidebar column sits beside the content, which uses the full width. A menu button is visible. The tiles stack in one or two columns, the chart fits inside the screen with no mark cut off and no axis labels running into each other, and the table is readable or scrolls inside its own box.
7. nav-phone: after tapping the menu button the navigation is open over the dashboard and shows Overview, Projects, Clients and Settings, in a panel that rises from the bottom edge of the screen (a bottom sheet, with rounded top corners, a heading and a close button) with a hairline edge and a soft glow or shadow with no hard offset. Its rows are tall enough to tap (about 44px), and the page behind is dimmed. If the navigation is not visible, fail this claim.
8. All screenshots: all text is regular weight (nothing bold), there are no emoji, no decorative gradients and no hard offset shadows, and no large flat accent fills: the chart marks, the tiles and the sidebar are not filled with the accent color, and no chart bar is the accent (the chart is foreground gray and black or white). The keyboard focus outline and the one soft light from the top (litt's light source, a faint tint that fades down a surface, once per view) are allowed. In the dark screenshots the tiles, chart and table are set off from the page by a hairline and a fill at least slightly lighter than the page, and all text is legible.
